subject: cuckoo wasp
title: This Wasp Breaks Into Other Wasps' Nests and Eats Their Babies

scenes.text: This wasp gets caught breaking in. It doesn't fight back.
The cuckoo wasp sneaks into other wasps' nests while the owner is away.
When the owner catches it, it curls into a tight ball, like a pill bug.
Its thick, pitted armor shrugs off stings and bites. The host can only carry it outside.
Unharmed, it turns around and walks right back in to lay its eggs.
Its larva eats the host's baby, then the food stored for it. The ball wins.

description:
Cuckoo wasps (family Chrysididae, over 3,000 species) slip into the nests of solitary bees and wasps to lay their eggs. When a host catches one, it curls into a tight ball whose thick, pitted armor resists stings and bites.
The host usually just carries it out, and the cuckoo wasp often goes straight back in. Its larva eats the host's egg or young, then the stored food.
What's the sneakiest parasite you know?
first_comment: Some cuckoo wasps hitch a ride into the burrow on the prey the host is dragging home. Which insect is the best burglar?
